chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Sari ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wants good for a servant, He hastens his punishment in the world; and when He wants evil for a servant, He withholds his sins until he meets them on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: Why does God punish believers in this world but delay punishment for others until the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi is often interpreted through the lens of divine mercy, where worldly trials serve as a purifying mechanism to clear the servant's ledger before the Hereafter. The contrast highlights that the absence of immediate punishment is not necessarily a sign of divine favor but can be a 'delayed settlement' (istidrāj) where sins accumulate for a greater reckoning. This concept underscores the importance of maintaining humility during periods of ease, recognizing that current tranquility may be a prelude to a more comprehensive accounting on the Day of Judgment.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Sary Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Wants good with a servant, would Hasten his Punishment to him in the world; and whenever He<sup>azwj</sup> Wants Wrath upon a servant, would Withhold (Punishment) from him for his sins until He<sup>azwj</sup> gets these to be fulfilled with on the Day of Judgment’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Sariy ibn Khalid from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, wants good for a servant He hastens his punishment in this world. When He wants evil for a servant He preserves his sins for him to find their consequences on the Day of Judgment.”
